summary.headline: Bajaj Electricals Q2 FY27: revenue up only ~1.5%, but EBIT margin rose 140 bps to 4.4% and PBT rose to INR35 crore from INR15 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue grew a modest ~1.5% YoY, led by Consumer Products (+2.4%), while Lighting Solutions degrew 1.3%. Gross margin held at 31.9% (management also cited 32.1% vs 31.4% YoY), and EBIT margin improved to 4.4% from 3.0%, with PBT more than doubling to INR35 crore from INR15 crore. Brand investment rose to 3.8% of revenue (+150 bps YoY), so like-for-like EBIT margin was stated at 5.9% vs 3.0%. Management also announced Chairman Shekhar Bajaj steps down from executive role at calendar year-end, with Sudarshan Sampathkumar becoming Non-Executive Independent Chairman from 1 January 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Gross margin up 10 bps QoQ; 32.1% vs 31.4% YoY (~70 bps)

financial_highlights.metric: EBIT margin like-for-like (ex incremental brand spend)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR15 crore YoY (more than doubled)

financial_highlights.metric: PBT margin ex incremental brand spend

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: Revenue +2.4% YoY, driven by induction cookers, water heaters and steam irons (high double-digit growth); ceiling fans declined more than double digits. EBIT margin 4% (5.6% like-for-like vs 2.8%).

segments.name: Lighting Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue -1.3% YoY on professional lighting decline of close to double digits (lost bids, selective pricing). Consumer lighting grew double digits on wires and switchgear (switchgear +28% on small base). EBIT margin 3.1%.

segments.name: E-commerce and exports
segments.commentary: E-commerce grew in double digits; export focus showed 'very strong growth' (no figures given).

segments.name: New categories (wires, switches)
segments.commentary: Management says new businesses are about 20-25% of consumer lighting; wires launched Feb 2026, focused on four states; no revenue run-rate disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Target: grow double digits, ahead of market (e.g., 10% if market grows 8%; 8% if market grows 6%).

Profitability aspiration: close to double-digit EBITDA/EBIT margin over time; timing (FY28 'may or may not be') depends on inflation and reinvestment; may accept high double-digit top line at lower profitability to invest in growth.
Chairman expects to surpass the highest-ever EBITDA (cited as ~INR320 crore, possibly INR300 crore, in FY21 for Consumer Products) within 2-3 years.

Price hike: one round taken in lighting in October 2026; a Consumer Products price increase is under evaluation and 'seems to be the case'. Policy: less than half of inflation to be passed through pricing.
Fan BLDC capacity expansion expected to take 3-6 months (capacity) and 4-5 months (new BLDC technology in factories).
capex_capacity: BLDC fan production capacity being augmented multifold; expected to be in place in next 3-6 months.
New-tech BLDC capability being built in factories, taking another 4-5 months.
BLDC fan launched on a limited-market basis; expanding to other states; national-level picture expected in about two quarters.
Wires business to be built with incremental consumer distribution and sales capability in a few focused states; described as needing continuous investment.
demand_pricing: Fans: declined more than double digits YoY; management attributes this to a legacy entry-level sub-economy fan portfolio, distribution losses in FY22-23, and late entry into BLDC.
Premium fans (induction plus BLDC) are over 30% of ceiling fan contribution; BLDC average operating price about INR2,500-3,000.
Channel: channel health 'improved materially'; management says inventory is disciplined, and last year's Q3 channel correction was exited with higher-than-desired channel inventory.

Pricing: prudent price hikes used as last resort; some volume softness in core categories with mix of price-led and volume-led growth by category; management prioritising quality of growth over discounting or channel loading.
Competition: management says the company is #1 or #2 in most categories and gaining or holding share except fans; an analyst cited peers Crompton and Orient Electric with higher growth and margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Consumer Products growth an outlier versus Havells, Crompton and TTK, and how is channel consolidation progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fans declined more than double digits and are dragging the average; net of fans, CP grew double digits across categories. BLDC is being scaled up with capacity to be in place in 3-6 months. No secondary sales numbers were shared.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the non-BLDC fan category declining so sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Portfolio was skewed to entry-level sub-economy fans where industry growth is weak. The focus has shifted to BLDC innovation and growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution of new categories in consumer lighting and where is the focus?
qa_highlights.answer: New businesses are about 20-25% of the total; focus is on four states where the brand is strong and the market is large. Professional lighting declined close to double digits due to lost bids and selective bidding amid inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CP margin trajectory and pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Water heaters have better margins than fans; management is optimistic on margin improvement without giving forward guidance. One lighting price increase was taken in October and a CP price increase is under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY28 targets for growth and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is growth ahead of market by about 2 percentage points, with close to double-digit profitability over time; FY28 timing is not committed. The company may invest behind growth, accepting lower margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the channel inventory status and the wires revenue run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel inventory is described as disciplined and healthy, with no inventory correction planned. Wires volumes are growing month-on-month; no run-rate or target figure was disclosed.

risks_watch: Fans: continued decline until BLDC capacity and national rollout are in place (3-6 months); the market-share recovery is unproven.
Input cost inflation in metals and plastics; further price hikes may be needed, with volume risk.
Professional lighting decline (close to double digits) from bid losses and selective bidding; order slowdown acknowledged.
Brand spend at 3.8% of revenue; margin progress depends on how much is reinvested versus retained.
Leadership transition: Chairman steps down at end-2026; new Non-Executive Independent Chairman from 1 January 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and cost control, but cautious and defensive on top-line growth; management acknowledged fans as the main drag and gave no firm timeline for the fan recovery. Responses on FY28 targets were hedged ('may or may not be FY28'), and detailed wires run-rate and category data were withheld.
key_quotes: We delivered modest revenue growth of hardly 1.5%. While our revenue growth was modest, we were able to maintain our gross margin of 31.9%.
So if you turn around fan, then you will see a very different number.
We want to grow double digit ahead of the market.
Our priorities remain clear: driving premiumization and innovations, optimizing the distribution, strengthening consumer engagement and continue to invest in our business with discipline.

adds.what: BLDC fan production capacity augmented multifold

growth.why: Management targets double-digit revenue growth (10% if market grows 8%, 8% if 6%) and says BLDC capacity is being built multifold, live in 3-6 months, but Q2 revenue grew only ~1.5% and fans declined more than double digits, so the guidance is only partly backed by specific capacity and timing.

roles: Chairman (Shekhar Bajaj steps down from executive role; Sudarshan Sampathkumar becomes Non-Executive Independent Chairma
mgmt.note: Shekhar Bajaj steps down from executive role at calendar year-end 2026; Sudarshan Sampathkumar becomes Non-Executive Independent Chairman from 1 January 2027, with no stated growth plan of his own.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBIT margin rose 140 bps YoY to 4.4% (5.9% like-for-like ex brand spend vs 3.0%), gross margin 31.9%, but brand spend is 3.8% of revenue (+150 bps) and management hedged on FY28 timing, so expansion depends on reinvestment and inflation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: BLDC fan capacity being augmented multifold, expected in place in 3-6 months; new-tech BLDC capability in factories takes another 4-5 months; wires build-out in focus states is ongoing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew only ~1.5% in Q2 with fans down more than double digits and professional lighting down close to double digits, while CP ex-fans grew double digits and BLDC grew 56% from a small base; recovery is unproven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it is building BLDC capacity multifold and wires needs continuous investment, but no new plant or utilisation figure was disclosed, so a fresh capex announcement is not firmly signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held a double-digit growth target (10% if market grows 8%) but Q2 revenue grew only ~1.5%, so an upgrade is hard to justify in the window.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management cut its margin timing to a hedged 'may or may not be FY28' and fan recovery has no firm timeline; revenue growth of ~1.5% sits well below the 8-10% target, and input cost inflation in metals and plastics is flagged.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BLDC fan launch is limited-market and expanding to other states with national picture in about two quarters; wires launched Feb 2026 and are being scaled in four states.

rows.label: Consumer Products price hike under evaluation
rows.why: One lighting price round taken in Oct 2026 and a CP increase 'seems to be the case', but management says less than half of inflation will be passed through and prices are a last resort, with some volume softness in core categories.

rows.label: Fan segment recovery via BLDC
rows.why: Fans fell more than double digits and BLDC is 17% of CP portfolio growing 56% YoY (26% YTD); BLDC capacity live in 3-6 months, but the market-share recovery is unproven.

rows.label: Professional lighting bid recovery
rows.why: Professional lighting fell close to double digits on lost bids and selective bidding amid inflation, and order slowdown was acknowledged, so no near-term rebound is signalled.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin and cost control (5.9% like-for-like EBIT margin) and on BLDC capacity, but cautious and defensive on top-line growth, fan recovery timing and FY28 targets; analysts pushed on the lagging top line versus peers Crompton and Orient Electric and on channel data.
